lead.hed: Carrier Air Wing 9 closed a 10-month combat deployment aboard Abraham Lincoln
lead.insight: DVIDS reported that Carrier Air Wing 9 concluded the deployment aboard USS Abraham Lincoln on Oct. 8, after embarking Nov. 21, 2025. The release says the wing flew 14,037 sorties and 31,460 flight hours, and that Operation Epic Fury, ordered Feb. 28, ran 38 days before an early April ceasefire. It says the wing expended 1,499 precision weapons, more than 1.37 million pounds of ordnance, against U.S. Central Command targets. Capt. J.W. Stigi, the wing commander, said the force destroyed Iran's conventional Navy and secured maritime chokepoints. Destroyers Spruance and Michael Murphy remain underway in the 7th and 5th Fleets. The still shows an F-35C from Marine Fighter Attack Squadron 314 on the flight deck Oct. 1, while the ship was still in the 3rd Fleet.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Angel Campbell · DVIDS 9996294 · Public domain · An F-35C from VMFA-314 prepares to launch from USS Abraham Lincoln in the U.S. 3rd Fleet. Photo taken Oct. 1, 2026.

political.hed: Heritage says restoring the Columbus fountain is a test of how the country treats its past
political.insight: Friday's commentary points to the Christopher Columbus fountain in front of Union Station in Washington, left in disrepair, as a case of history treated as something to neglect. The writer says restoring public artwork can put life back into a culture, and that the fountain is a reminder of the country's tie to the old world. It is a commentary on public memory, not a restoration contract.

political.hed: American Reformer says Ohio is a place, not a slogan
political.insight: Friday's essay argues that national commentary flattens Ohio into a symbol and misses the practical judgments people there actually make. The writer wants fewer generalizations and more attention to how a particular place works. It is an argument about political writing, not a campaign filing.

tech.hed: Lockheed unveiled a PAC-3 variant aimed at hypersonic threats
tech.insight: Defense News, citing Reuters, reported Saturday that Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge, an interceptor meant to counter hypersonic and advanced missile threats at longer ranges and higher altitudes. The company said it adds a new seeker, upgraded flight controls, and a multi-pulse rocket motor from Northrop Grumman. Tim Cahill, president of missiles and fire control, told Reuters the cost should be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE, and that full production would run about 2,000 a year. The Army awarded Lockheed a contract worth up to $58.6 billion in July to ramp up current PAC-3 production. This is a company unveiling, not a signed order for the new variant.

tech.hed: The Defense Department identified 250 missing service members in fiscal 2026
tech.insight: A DVIDS release from Washington says the Department of War identified 250 service members in fiscal year 2026, a record, under the accounting mission that treats no fallen comrade as left behind. The release is the official count posted this week. It does not list the individual cases.

culture.hed: Heritage says a $3 billion gift does not fix a campus that protects hate
culture.insight: Friday's commentary says Ken Griffin's $3 billion gift to Carnegie Mellon, most of it for a new Miami campus, is the largest single gift in American higher education. The writer says cash was not the school's problem. Nearly a month after an associate's conduct drew public attention, the piece argues federal and donor money still flows to campuses that shelter antisemitism. It is an argument about funding conditions, not a new statute.

culture.hed: TruthScript says the fight over the unsupervised woman misses Christian vocation
culture.insight: Thursday's essay says the latest evangelical argument over a figure called the unsupervised woman asks the wrong question. The writer argues the dispute treats women's work as a supervision problem and skips what Christian vocation actually requires of women and men. It is a theological argument, not a church court ruling.

watch.hed: Ships in the Strait of Hormuz have been hit nearly every day this month
watch.note: USNI News, Friday. The International Maritime Organization count is nine ships from Oct. 1 through Tuesday, mostly commercial. No official still on this board.

watch.hed: Philippine and Chinese incidents rose in the South China Sea and the Luzon Strait
watch.note: USNI News, Friday. The story cites a Philippine Coast Guard photo of a China Coast Guard cutter near Batanes on Oct. 1. Outlet art, not staged as the lead.
